title: A case of White-Sutton syndrome with previously described loss-of-function variant in DDE domain of POGZ (p.Arg1211*) and Kartagener syndrome

reviewer.method: Read the complete published two-page correspondence, including all references; inspected both rendered pages and every Figure 1 panel; compared the sole alternate packet, all 18 phenotype items and its allele descriptor.

audit.exposure_note: Parent inherited aggregate benchmark results and historical per-case public-control narratives before this review. No target-case inference output was opened for this review. Conservatively per_case, post-inference and not blinded.

artifacts.description: Publisher version, Am J Med Genet A 2021;185A:1006–1007, DOI 10.1002/ajmg.a.62042; two complete physical pages.
Complete pdftotext -layout extraction; read through the final reference and checked against both page images.
Rendered complete printed page 1006, including Figure 1 panels a–c; inspected.
Rendered complete printed page 1007, including discussion, disclosures and entire reference list; inspected.
Authorized UOC institutional retrieval receipt; acquisition alone is not reading.

identity.note: Complete publisher correspondence verified from title, DOI, author list and contiguous printed pages 1006–1007; not the Pascolini article discussed in its opening paragraphs.

evidence.locator: Both complete pages 1006–1007: one Figure 1 with panels a–c, no table or supplemental-item citation; p1007 concludes with full references.

component_inventory.note: The complete two-page correspondence contains one three-panel figure and no tables or supplements. The publisher full-article page was also inspected and showed no Supporting Information section. No supplemental material is cited in the article.

extent_evidence.locator: Complete extraction from both PDF pages; all lines counted.

coverage.locator: Lines 1–119, including references, captions, disclosures and footer; cross-checked against both rendered pages.

components.note: Complete text read; column order resolved by visual inspection of both printed pages.

extent_evidence.locator: p1006 Figure 1, labelled panels a, b, c.

coverage.locator: p1006 lower half: all Figure 1 panels a–c and caption inspected at 1800-pixel page rendering.

components.note: Panels a/b are frontal images in infancy and at five years; c is a lateral view. Detailed HPO diagnoses are not inferred from photographs alone.

limitations: Full source review complete, but 11 detailed phenotype assertions lack explicit source confirmation.
One photograph-based feature is qualified; exact transcript/genomic normalization and documented parental testing remain unavailable.
The proposed Kartagener association is not proven; the authors retain a possible unknown alternative genotype.

patient_identity.statement: The packet identifies the single 19-year-old male case described by Dal et al.; age, sex, POGZ variant and WHSUS context match. This is not the previously published Pascolini case cited in the opening paragraphs.

evidence.locator: p1006 left final paragraph and right first paragraph; Figure 1 caption.

genotype.statement: The report identifies a de novo POGZ c.3631C>T (p.Arg1211*) loss-of-function variant by exome sequencing. The coding/protein description matches the packet, but the exact reference accessions, genomic assembly/coordinate and explicit heterozygous allele fraction are not printed.

evidence.locator: p1006 left final paragraph.

limitations: Source matching of coding/protein notation does not independently validate the packet NM_015100.4, NP_055915.2, GRCh38 coordinate or zygosity normalization.

segregation.statement: The authors state that the POGZ variant is de novo; the correspondence supplies neither parental genotypes nor a pedigree or parentage-testing method.

evidence.locator: p1006 left final paragraph; complete pp1006–1007.

limitations: Reported de novo status is source-supported, not independently demonstrated by available segregation data.

phase.statement: The packet has one POGZ variant and the report describes one de novo allele. Multi-variant cis/trans phase is not required for this source match and is not measured in the article.

evidence.locator: p1006 left final paragraph.

limitations: Do not reinterpret a single-allele narrative as experimental phasing or an allele-fraction measurement.

causal_confidence.statement: The authors consider the truncating POGZ allele consistent with WHSUS and propose an expanded association with Kartagener-like findings. They explicitly retain an unknown alternative genotype. Ciliary ultrastructure was not confirmed because sampling was nondiagnostic; a ciliary dyskinesia panel and SNP microarray were reported normal.

evidence.locator: p1006 right first paragraph; p1007 left discussion, final sentence.

limitations: Single case correspondence; no direct POGZ functional rescue or established causal attribution of the ciliary phenotype. Packet SOLVED/CAUSATIVE/PATHOGENIC labels are not independent validation.

phenotype_completeness.statement: All 18 positive packet features were reviewed; none is encoded as excluded. The packet omits explicitly reported micropenis, gynecomastia, cutis marmorata, morbid obesity, bilateral slipped capital femoral epiphysis, obstructive sleep apnoea, dextrocardia and clinical ciliary dysfunction. The report gives age 19 at presentation and photographs from infancy and age five, without individual onset ages for all packet items.

evidence.locator: p1006 case narrative and Figure 1 caption; p1007 discussion.

limitations: The packet is a selective phenotype representation, not a complete case record; omitted findings and unconfirmed ciliary ultrastructure remain material.

assessment.statement: POGZ c.3631C>T and p.Arg1211* agree with the article. The packet adds NM_015100.4, NP_055915.2, NC_000001.11:g.151405404G>A, hg38 chr1:151405404 G>A and heterozygous status; those exact normalization/zygosity details are not supplied by this correspondence.

evidence.locator: p1006 left final paragraph.

limitations: Transcript and genomic-coordinate normalization remain unverified against this source; no allelic read counts are reported.

evidence.locator: p1006 right first paragraph; Figure 1 caption as applicable.

assessment.statement: The mouth is visibly open in frontal Figure 1 panels a and b, which supports the appearance encoded by the packet. The prose instead describes tented lips.

evidence.locator: Figure 1 panels a–b on p1006.

limitations: A photographed appearance does not establish persistent open-mouth posture or its mechanism.

assessment.statement: The source reports tented lips, but does not explicitly identify downturned mouth corners. The full narrative, figure and caption were checked.
